correctness.summary: The lower bound reduces total domination within each rooted C_{4k+1} copy to a vertex cover of an odd path. The unique minimum cover forces every minimum-cost copy into one local pattern, so all cross-copy obligations reduce to a locating-dominating set of the base graph. The matching upper construction uses complementary low/high periodic patterns and a minimum locating-dominating set of the base. All total-domination and locating cases have been checked explicitly.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Wei et al. (2020) state a different exact formula for the path-by-cycle case q1 congruent to 1 modulo 4. Targeted searches under locating-total/location-total, rooted-product and comb-product terminology found no correction of that case or the general identity. The 2020 comb-product paper located in the search concerns ordinary locating domination, not locating-total domination. Residual risk remains from alternate terminology or poorly indexed corrections.

value.summary: The result corrects a published exact formula by a substantive amount and replaces it with a general identity for arbitrary connected base graphs. It also gives a parameter-preserving embedding of ordinary locating domination into locating-total domination on a natural rooted-product family.

limitations: Only cycle lengths 4k+1 are treated by the new theorem.
The theorem transfers gamma_L(H) rather than evaluating it for arbitrary base graphs.
The finite optimization checks are corroborative and not part of the proof.
No claim is made about the validity of unrelated results in the 2020 source.
